newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends '96 at record, up 11.7 pct for year.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends '96 at record, up 11.7 pct for year.

text.p: Leading UK blue chips ended 1996 at a fresh closing high, chalking up an annual gain of 11.6 percent, and most strategists said they were looking for further gains in 1997.

The leading FTSE 100 settled at 4,118.5, up 2.8 points, having set a new intraday peak of 4,123.2 earlier. Volume was thin, with only 172.4 million shares recorded by 1242 GMT on this holiday shortened session.
It was the third consecutive session the index climbed to a record intraday high.
According to a Reuters poll, nine of the 13 brokerages surveyed were expecting the FTSE 100 to end 1997 above current levels. Estimates were as high as 4,500 and as low as 4,000.

"It'll be a choppy first quarter with political uncertainties coming to a head and then we'll get on with it," said SocGen UK equity strategist Andy Hartwill, whose 1997 year-end forecast was 4,250 -- the mean estimate.
"Growth rates will pick up and possibly peak in 1997, interest rates will rise, and the FTSE 100 will finish the year higher than it is today, but we'll probably take the scenic route," he added.
Earnings growth along with continued merger and acquisition activity, particularly in the financial and utility sectors, should fuel the rally during the latter part of the of 1997, he said.

Today's advance to the record intraday high was tied to the expiration of over-the-counter (OTC) FTSE 100 index "flex options," dealers said. They expired just after 1000 GMT, bringing a few minutes of activity to an otherwise dull market.
"We saw some year-end FTSE flex OTC's expire which gave the cash market a brief boost. The FTSE futures spiked up a bit, taking the cash market higher," said one options trader.
Flex options are similar to FTSE 100 index options but the strike and expiration dates are established "over-the-counter" between buyer and seller.
Later this afternoon, the Chicago Purchasing Managers December survey, the December consumer confidence survey and November new home sales will be published.
